policy_title: Empower Local Authorities to End Right to Buy
stated: Giving local authorities, including National Park Authorities, the powers to end Right to Buy in their areas.

source.quote: Giving local authorities, including National Park Authorities, the powers to end Right to Buy in their areas.

bearing_set.reason: Right to Buy directly reduces social housing stock; enabling local authorities to end it would preserve affordable/social tenure supply, with a non-negligible effect on housing availability and affordability for lower-income households.

membership_note: The policy has one clean, non-negligible bearing: O1. A secondary O14 (inequality) mechanism exists in theory — council tenants (typically lower-income) lose a discounted route to homeownership — but given current RTB sales are historically low (circa 2,000–3,000/year vs 200,000+/year in the 1980s), the near-term distributional effect does not clear the non-negligible bar; the dominant effect remains stock preservation. No O10 bearing: RTB is a state-conferred statutory right, not a natural property right, so its removal does not constitute state coercion or interference with property already held. No O13 bearing: aggregate living-standards/mobility effect is too diffuse to pin to a specific indicator at current RTB volumes.
